title: Rust Language Indexing Support
description: Roadmap for making Rust language indexing useful beyond structural TS-indexed fallback.

decisions.q: How do we avoid losing explore/exploit work while starting Rust indexing?
decisions.answer: Track all known explore and exploit branches in the roadmap now. Start implementation with bounded Rust core ownership for .rs files, while keeping module paths, traits, macros, Cargo workspace/features, framework routes, validation, and product surface as explicit nodes.
decisions.note: This prevents the first implementation slice from silently redefining full Rust language support.

1-1.label: Rust language support baseline and taxonomy

decisions.q: What is the current Rust language indexing boundary?
decisions.answer: Current .rs support is Rust-owned baseline structural indexing through rust-hybrid. Full Rust semantic graph work remains explicitly tracked under 1-4.
decisions.note: This supersedes the initial pre-Plan-1 audit where .rs still used the mature TypeScript indexer path.

decisions.q: What is the current Rust language indexing boundary after Plan 1?
decisions.answer: Current .rs support is Rust-owned baseline structural indexing through rust-hybrid. Full Rust semantic graph work remains explicitly tracked under 1-4.

1-1.notes: Initial baseline/taxonomy discussion superseded by Plan 1 implementation; remaining semantic gaps are tracked under 1-4.

decisions.q: Should the first implementation slice make Rust core own .rs baseline extraction?
decisions.answer: Yes. First add bounded Rust core .rs baseline extraction and rust-hybrid ownership; do not include trait coherence, macro expansion, Cargo feature resolution, or compiler-grade semantics in this slice.
decisions.note: This creates the foundation for later Rust semantic graph slices without pretending the first slice completes full Rust language intelligence.

decisions.q: What is included in the first Rust language indexing implementation slice?
decisions.answer: Accept bounded baseline extraction: Rust core owns .rs files for basic structure, imports, and calls. Exclude trait dispatch, macro expansion, Cargo feature resolution, and compiler-grade Rust semantics.
decisions.note: Those deeper semantics remain tracked under 1-4 Rust semantic graph slices.

decisions.q: Which GitHub issues implement Rust core .rs ownership Plan 1?
decisions.answer: #566 covers parser ownership; #567 covers baseline .rs graph extraction; #568 covers rust-hybrid .rs assignment and diagnostics; #569 covers validation, guardrails, and evidence.
decisions.note: Published with enhancement + ready-for-agent labels in dependency order.

decisions.answer: Rust core now owns .rs baseline parsing/extraction and rust-hybrid includes rust in Rust-owned languages. Deeper Rust semantic graph work remains under 1-4.
